name: Passive Voice Frequency
description: Calculates the sheer density and distribution of passive verbs. Due to safety-alignment, artificial neutrality, and a tendency to avoid committing to a specific perspective, AI models default to passive constructions over active ones, resulting in a significantly higher and more uniform frequency of passive voice than human writing.
algorithm: Auxiliary Verb Dependency and Passive Density Mapping
mechanism: This algorithm scans the text using dependency parsing, specifically isolating 'auxiliary verb + past participle' structures (e.g., 'was observed', 'is considered') that lack a direct acting subject. It calculates the overall frequency of these constructions per 1,000 words. Large Language Models (LLMs) are rigorously fine-tuned to maintain an objective, authoritative, and non-committal tone—traits heavily associated with the passive voice. Consequently, when an AI generates an essay, report, or summary, it naturally gravitates toward passive sentence structures. Human writers, even in formal contexts, use the passive voice sparingly and purposefully (typically to emphasize the object of an action rather than the actor). The system computes a 'Passive Saturation Score' by measuring the raw frequency of passive verbs against established baselines for specific genres. A high density of passive constructions distributed uniformly across the text points strongly to machine generation.
useCase: Highly useful for auditing academic papers, business reports, and news summaries, detecting the sterile, 'safe', and artificially objective tone symptomatic of AI generation.
strengths:
• Directly targets a known stylistic bias in LLMs caused by their alignment training (RLHF).
• Provides an easily interpretable, mathematically objective metric.
• highly consistent across different AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini).
limitations:
• Yields false positives on human-written legal texts, medical journals, and rigid laboratory reports where passive voice is an industry standard.
• Easily bypassed by simple prompt engineering (e.g., 'rewrite this using active voice entirely').
• Cannot be used accurately on very short texts where statistical density cannot be established.
parameters:
Analysis: Dependency Parsing for Auxiliary+Participle Structures
Metric: Passive Verb Frequency per 1,000 Words and Paragraph Uniformity
Output: 0-100 Passive Saturation (Artificial Objectivity) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-75% accuracy. Best used as a supplementary feature within a broader text analysis pipeline rather than a standalone definitive metric.

references.title: Herbold, S. et al. (2023). A Large-Scale Comparison of Human-Written Versus ChatGPT-Generated Essays. Scientific Reports.
Biber, D. (1988). Variation Across Speech and Writing. Cambridge University Press.
